rsm.bootstrap_type: residual (fixed-design); case bootstrap reported for comparison

achieved_predictor_sensitivity.note: primary refit; source Methods used achieved flow/temp

curve_band.units: cup mass (g) at central achieved (F,T); iid residual bootstrap

rsm_diagnostics.conditional_on: selected seven-term achieved-predictor specification (post-selection uncertainty disclosed separately)
rsm_diagnostics.verdict: The conditional grind vertex ~1.74 is stable to single-RUN (1.736-1.765) and single-SETTING (1.720-1.776, 15/15 concave-in-domain) deletion and to a full-quadratic form (vertex 1.737; retained-7 AICc -196.6 < full -189.7). Wild bootstraps (Rademacher [1.6997, 1.7421, 1.829], Mammen [1.6934, 1.7441, 1.818]) preserve the vertex while modestly widening vs the iid residual interval [1.6992, 1.7434, 1.8174] -- so the conditional vertex is NOT an artefact of iid resampling despite the ~17x within-setting SD range. All intervals condition on the selected seven-term model.
rsm_diagnostics.strength: conditional (fixed-specification) deletion + wild-bootstrap + AICc model-form sensitivity; NOT post-selection or unconditional inference

rsm_lopo.caveat: 15 settings held out with all reps together; achieved predictors; small n, diagnostic not power-backed; pressure is NOT an RSM factor

result1.experimental_unit_note: Each dial setting was run as independently prepared extraction repetitions (1.4 axis n=3, 1.7 centre n=6, 2.0 axis n=3); those runs are the experimental unit, so the within-cell spread is run-to-run variance at a fixed NOMINAL dial (review MAJ-03). There is NO replication across machines/coffees/campaigns (one machine, one coffee), so a replicate-level Welch/trend test is a within-campaign, setting-level contrast conditional on run independence -- NOT a causal 'dial alone moves EY' claim; a design-aware model would need the full DoE (achieved covariates + experiment blocks), not these 3 selected cells.
result1.achieved_confound: achieved flow/temperature/max-pressure differ across the three dial experiments (see cells) -> dial is confounded with the achieved conditions; the ordering is descriptive, not a clean dial effect.
result1.verdict: observed cell means increase monotonically (18.27 -> 19.38 -> 19.62 EY%); the MIDDLE dial is below the coarse end -> NO middle-dial maximum in the observed means. Described as ORDERED, not 'statistically monotone' (see the 1.4-vs-1.7 CI). Achieved covariates differ across the three selected settings.

channeling_audit.verdict: EY(k) is concave over 96-97% of the tested support and the lognormal clip mass is <0.16% at all grinds/pressures; the DIRECT Jensen gap J=E[EY(K)]-EY(E[K_eval]) -- using the ACTUAL post-clipping evaluated mean (shift from unity <=0.0051, review MAJ-17) not EY(1) -- is <=0 in every cell (deficit -4.636 to -1.379 EY-pt, worst = most negative) -> the ensemble deficit is confirmed by direct measurement, not only by the 2nd-derivative sign (global concavity NOT claimed); clipping is negligible.

ladder.discrimination_reading: time variation is NEEDED (all constant nulls >=0.57 vs Phi(t) 0.12); a 4-param flexible curve reaches 0.10, so the ladder establishes NEED for time variation, not a specific bed mechanism -- the mechanistic content is a poroelastic Phi(t) with no coefficient fitted to the scored trace (though target-informed upstream) approaching the same-trace descriptive benchmark

result2_residuals.verdict: Block bootstrap (~8 s blocks, respecting the strong residual autocorrelation -- lag-1 ACF 1.00 for Phi(t)): Phi(t) beats the best constant by -0.391 g/s (95% [-0.6, -0.226], excludes 0 = True), but only TIES the 4-param cubic (diff 0.022, 95% [-0.008, 0.053], excludes 0 = False). The Phi-over-constant advantage persists across the 10-90/15-95/20-90 s windows (True). Under block-length sensitivity (4/8/16/24 s) the Phi>const advantage is stable at every block length (True), while the Phi~cubic TIE is borderline (stable = False: the longest block marginally favors the cubic) -- if anything the flexible null does at least as well as Phi. So time variation robustly reduces IN-SAMPLE reconstruction error over constants, but a flexible non-mechanistic curve does equally well -- not predictive mechanism identification.
result2_residuals.strength: dependence-aware (moving-block bootstrap) RMSE-difference uncertainty + window sensitivity; IN-SAMPLE reconstruction, not held-out prediction

cross_pressure.reading: Phi(t) has the lowest transfer-mean RMSE, but no single mechanism is lowest at every pressure (descriptively: RC-3b lower at low P, static lower mid-range). These are DESCRIPTIVE summaries of the continuous pressure-residual curve, not pre-registered physical regimes; the physical origin of the pattern is unresolved. Conditional-transfer, NOT independent validation.

loco.strength: within-rig leave-one-pressure-out held-out prediction (one campaign/coffee/grind; 2-param equilibrium pair refit) -- NOT independent second-rig out-of-sample validation
loco.reading: Leaving each pressure out and refitting the equilibrium pair moves (P_c,Q_c) by at most 2.8%, and the held-out RMSE matches the shared-calibration RMSE -- so the two-parameter equilibrium calibration is not dominated by any single pressure point. This does NOT establish that the residual pressure pattern is physical (review MAJ-14): the 9-bar solids trajectory and other donor assumptions remain fixed, so omitted machine dynamics, viscosity/sensor effects, an imperfect equilibrium form, or other omitted bed mechanisms could produce the same pattern. Its physical origin is unresolved.

ladder.note: rung1 and the cubic get their free parameters re-optimized per shot (their best case); rung3 and rung4 are zero-free-parameter predictions evaluated as-is. Phi(t) is NOT re-fitted per shot -- a true leave-one-shot-out cross-fit needs shot-matched TDS, which was never published (review 4.3/4.4 stays blocked).

noise_floor.note: Descriptive shot-to-shot scatter, not a fitted model and not an error bar on any rung. It is the scale on which RMSE DIFFERENCES between rungs should be judged.

paired.supersedes: within-curve block resampling of the mean trace, which is retained only as a secondary within-curve sensitivity
paired.note: Free parameters are re-optimized per shot for the constant and the cubic. Phi(t) and the static curve carry no free parameters here, but their upstream calibration is only partially cross-fitted (see leave_one_shot_out_phi).

remaining_target_reuse: dissolved_mass_sigmoid_k_l_m (TDS replicates are not shot-matched to the flow traces, so it cannot be rebuilt per held-out shot)
loso_phi.note: Partial cross-fit: the equilibrium channel IS withheld, the solids-sigmoid channel is not. Do NOT describe this as a leave-one-shot-out validation of Phi(t).

comparator.smoothing_selection: GCV on the training data only

heldout.leave_segment_out_caveat: the first and last segments require the spline to extrapolate beyond its support, where it is unstable; the interior mean is the interpolation question and is the headline
heldout.note: The spline never sees the points it is scored on under either protocol. The leave-one-shot-out spline is trained on the mean of the other four shots, which is the same object the manuscript scores, so the protocols are comparable.

window_sensitivity.note: The manuscript must NOT attribute a 110-120 s statistic to this analysis. The repository's equilibrium observable is the final 100 s value of each preprocessed pressure mean; it reproduces the published static fit. The nominal 110-120 s window is unusable from the published raw traces without an exclusion the source did not make (shot 9-1 has ended inside it).

residuals_1s.note: ACF and Durbin-Watson are computed on the SAME decimated series for every branch. Durbin-Watson near 2 indicates no lag-1 structure AT THIS RESOLUTION; the value changes with resolution, which is why the resolution is declared rather than implied.

residuals_5s.note: ACF and Durbin-Watson are computed on the SAME decimated series for every branch. Durbin-Watson near 2 indicates no lag-1 structure AT THIS RESOLUTION; the value changes with resolution, which is why the resolution is declared rather than implied.

recorded_pressure.note: Point-by-point substitution of the recorded basket pressure for the nominal setpoint; window, calibration, dissolution parameters and dose held fixed. A robustness result, not evidence for any mechanism.

pressure_domains.boundary_note: P_c = 12.39 bar sits just inside the tested range [1.0, 13.0]: only 1 of the 11 reference pressures reach or exceed it, so the saturating branch of the equilibrium curve is exercised by essentially one pressure and the rest of the campaign probes the sub-characteristic regime.
pressure_domains.conflation_hazard: The recorded basket pressure is systematically BELOW nominal at every setting (up to 0.61 bar). A statement about '9 bar' therefore means the nominal setting, not the delivered pressure of 8.71 bar.

ntube_robustness.design_type: OFAT sweeps + one crossed control×lateral×closure design (NOT a full factorial)
ntube_robustness.owed: physical transverse-Darcy lateral operator + formal Jacobian/finite-time-Lyapunov growth analysis (Result 3 stays exploratory until then)
ntube_robustness.verdict: OFAT sweeps (N 100-800, substeps 4-32, grind 1.1-2.0, pressure 6-11 bar, 16 stochastic realisations) + a crossed control×lateral×closure design: concentration is invariant on the NUMERICAL (True), STOCHASTIC (True), and OPERATING (True) axes, and is DELIBERATELY suppressed by the physical-contingency axes {ck-closure, lateral>0, pressure-control} -- the scientific finding, not a failure. Among concentrating configs N_eff_final in [1.0, 2.0] (N_eff/N in [0.0013, 0.0100]). Full-trajectory flow-share conservation + raw non-negativity hold (OK). This is a SWEEP + conservation robustness result in the tested family, NOT a proven instability -- a physical lateral operator + a formal finite-time-growth analysis remain owed, so Result 3 stays exploratory.

ntube_switching_convergence.verdict: Refining the Euler timestep 16x (substeps 4->64) at FIXED N=200 and output grid: the persistent single-channel onset lands in [2.60, 2.60] s (spread 0.0 s, converges=True), the final N_eff in [1.0, 1.0] (converges=True), and the N_eff(t) trajectory deviates from the finest run by at most 109.661 channels. So the early switching event is STABLE under Euler substep refinement at fixed spatial discretization/output grid -- NOT a proven grid-independent physical event: a higher-order/adaptive integrator, an N-refinement, and interpolated event times remain owed (B6-04/B5-08), and a physical lateral operator + formal growth analysis before any stability claim.
ntube_switching_convergence.strength: Euler-substep stability of the finite-time collapse EVENT at fixed N + output grid (physical clock); NOT a formal stability/eigenmode result and NOT full grid-independent trajectory convergence
